input.title: N06 — Treatment timeline during circulatory support
input.facts:
A 28-year-old man presented with circulatory shock. At 08:21 on Day 0, BP was 70/45 mmHg and heart rate 142 beats/min. Right-heart abnormalities and a femoral venous thrombus were identified. VA-ECMO started at 10:20. CT pulmonary angiography at 11:58 showed main/branch pulmonary arterial filling defects. These are extracts for a retrospective ICU record review, not a live treatment instruction.

Day-0 record:
Time | Record
11:55 | Sample: platelets 21 × 10⁹/L, haemoglobin 150 g/L, fibrinogen 1.18 g/L and aPTT 43.5 s. Result-reporting times are not supplied for this sample.
14:50–15:10 | Two institutional therapeutic doses of apheresis platelets were transfused. Other haemostatic support was recorded over 13:15–17:00.
17:00 | Unfractionated heparin (UFH) was paused and the first alteplase infusion started. No post-transfusion platelet count immediately before this infusion is supplied.
17:20 | Arterial cannulation-site bleeding was treated with compression.
17:39 | Sample: platelets 62 × 10⁹/L, haemoglobin 136 g/L, fibrinogen 1.38 g/L and aPTT 47.5 s. Result-reporting times are not supplied for this sample.
18:10 | Vasoactive infusion rates were reduced, but ECMO and vasoactive support were still needed.
19:03 | A progress note records cessation of cannulation-site bleeding after compression; a second alteplase dose was ordered.
19:25 | The second infusion started. Each infusion stage lasted approximately one hour; exact completion timestamps are unavailable.
20:13 | A coagulation sample was obtained: fibrinogen 1.07 g/L and aPTT 58.9 s.
21:06 | The coagulation results from the 20:13 sample were reported.

The treating team later reported that UFH restarted after the second infusion, approximately one hour after its 19:25 start. No independent exact restart timestamp is available. A patient-specific anticoagulation target and the documented evidence used at restart are not supplied. The subsequent clinical course and later safety adjudication are not supplied.
input.task: Audience: an ICU clinical case review. Write 180–240 words in English using the headings Timing, Evidence and risks, and Missing record. Reconstruct the approximate UFH restart time and label recorded versus derived times. Calculate the 20:13-to-report delay and compare reporting with the estimated restart, preserving uncertainty about the actual restart. Assess whether this record establishes that the aPTT 58.9 s result informed restart. Explain what the platelet measurements do and do not show about the count at first alteplase initiation or a subsequent treatment effect. Identify the most useful missing records for assessing the decisions and bleeding risk. Do not prescribe a regimen, convert unverified infusion rates, invent an exact completion/restart time, or infer safety from an outcome not supplied.

input.answer:
**Timing**
The second alteplase infusion began at 19:25 (recorded) and lasted approximately one hour, giving an estimated completion of ~20:25 (derived). The team later reported that UFH restarted "approximately one hour after" the 19:25 start, yielding an estimated restart of ~20:25 (derived); no independent exact timestamp is available. The 20:13 coagulation sample was reported at 21:06, a 53-minute delay. The estimated restart (~20:25) therefore precedes the result report (21:06) by roughly 41 minutes, meaning the aPTT value was not yet available when UFH was restarted.

**Evidence and risks**
Because the aPTT 58.9 s was reported after the estimated restart, this record does not establish that the result informed the restart decision. The 11:55 platelet count (21 × 10⁹/L) reflects the pre-transfusion baseline. The 17:39 count (62 × 10⁹/L) was drawn 39 minutes after the first alteplase began; it cannot confirm the count at initiation, nor isolate a transfusion effect from ongoing consumption or dilution.

**Missing record**
The most useful absent entries are: an exact UFH restart timestamp with the documented anticoagulation target and rationale; a platelet count drawn immediately before the first alteplase infusion; and the subsequent clinical course with safety adjudication.
